headline: Approved two-lot subdivisions at 24 Worthley Road and 190 Hampstead Road, plus escrows for 57 Crystal Avenue and 35 Maple Street.
summary: Nearby residents raised concerns about blasting, steep driveways, and runoff at 24 Worthley Road, and that plan passed 7-2 with conditions. A motion to call the Hampstead Road plan a development of regional impact failed 0-9. A review of zoning changes needed to match new state laws was tabled because the meeting ran late.
decisions: Approved cash escrow of $58,811.00 for 57 Crystal Avenue Site Redevelopment, 9-0.
Approved Escrow #26-38, Release #2 of $51,807.60 for Site Plan 35 Maple Street, 9-0.
Approved minutes of the October 7, 2026 meeting and the October 17, 2026 site walk, 7-0 with 2 abstentions.
Approved waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.B, setting lot size by lot area instead of soil type for 24 Worthley Road, 7-2.
Approved waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.A (2) on lot lines at right angles to streets for 24 Worthley Road, 9-0.
Approved waiver from LDCR Section 170-26.A (16.a.iv) on sight distance profile for new driveway, 9-0.
Approved waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.G on granite bounds where existing boundary markers would be impacted, 9-0.
Adopted findings of fact for the 24 Worthley Road subdivision, 7-2.
Approved two-lot subdivision at 24 Worthley Road under expedited review, with conditions, 7-2.
Motion to find the 190 Hampstead Road subdivision a development of regional impact failed 0-9.
Adopted findings of fact for the 190 Hampstead Road subdivision, 9-0.
Approved two-lot subdivision at 190 Hampstead Road under expedited review, with conditions, 9-0.
Tabled review of proposed Zoning Ordinance changes to match recent State legislative amendments.

transcript:
## Escrow

The Planning Board for the Town of Derry held a public meeting on Wednesday, November 04, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. The meeting was broadcast from the Derry Municipal Center, 14 Manning Street, Third Floor meeting room, with a virtual option.

Members present: Dave Nelson, Chair, John O'Connor, Vice Chair, Randy Chase, Town Council Liaison, Brian Chirichiello, Town Administrator Representative, Bryan Fishman, Jacob Pelletier, and Derek Minervini, Members, and Thomas Mauzy, Z. Michael Appleton, and Andrew Young, Alternates

Members absent: Richard Malaby, Secretary, and Michael Wood, Member

Also present: Elizabeth Robidoux, Planning Director, and Caroline Wilson, Planning Administrative Secretary II

Mr. Nelson opened the meeting at 7:00 p.m. The meeting began with a salute to the flag.

Mr. Young was seated for Mr. Wood, and Mr. Appleton was seated for Mr. Malaby.

Mr. Pelletier was seated as Secretary Pro-Tem.

**#26-37**

**Project Name: 57 Crystal Avenue Site Redevelopment**

**Developer: Cafua Realty Trust CLXXIII, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Cash Escrow**

**Parcel ID/Location: 36017-001, 57 Crystal Avenue**

The request is to establish cash escrow in the amount of $58,811.00, for the above noted project. This escrow will be non-interest bearing.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, to approve Escrow #26-37 as presented.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

**#26-38**

**Project Name: Site Plan 35 Maple Street**

**Developer: Hornes Pond Real Estate Group, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Letter of Credit**

**Parcel ID/Location: 29151, 35 Maple Street**

The request is to approve Release #2 against Letter of Credit # 24284, drawn on Enterprise Bank, for the above noted project, and request a replacement letter of credit in the amount of $30,721.68.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, to approve Escrow #26-38 as presented.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

## Minutes

The Board reviewed the minutes of the October 07, 2026 public meeting and the minutes of the October 17, 2026 public site walk of PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, to approve the minutes of the October 07, 2026 public meeting and the minutes of the October 17, 2026 public site walk of PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road as written.
>
> Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Chirichiello, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. Fishman and Pelletier abstained due to being absent from both meetings. The motion passed.

## Correspondence

Mr. Pelletier reported the Board received the quarterly Change of Use spreadsheet, which lists several new businesses and some ownership changes. The new edition of the NHMA Town and City Magazine is now available.

## Other Business

### Housing Readiness Pilot Update – James Vayo, AICP

Ms. Robidoux introduced Mr. Vayo, a Planner with Southern NH Planning Commission (SNHPC). Derry is involved in a pilot project with SNHPC which examines housing readiness. Derry was selected because we have three distinct areas: urban, suburban, and rural. The results of this project will inform Derry and the other communities in the SNHPC regions on items they may wish to consider as models for housing.

Mr. Vayo explained the Pilot was made possible by a grant from Housing and Urban Development (HUD). All nine of the State's Planning Commissions were awarded the funding. The objective is to help facilitate each Commission's Regional Comprehensive Plan (RCP) and Housing Needs Assessment.

Three bodies of work have been completed thus far: 1. A survey of residents and others within Derry, 2. An analysis of existing conditions for each of the three distinct areas, and 3. A regulatory crosswalk. The fourth item which remains to be done is conceptual planning on select sites.

The three cross-section areas are: Area 1 - Downtown, Area 2 – Route 28/Ryan's Hill, and Area 3 – Route 102/Chester Road.

The survey asked residents and others to provide input on the following housing types: accessory dwelling units (ADUs), clustered apartments, townhouses, cottage courts, 3-story mixed-use, live-work, duplex/triplex, and apartment houses.

188 individuals responded to the survey from June 16-July 12, 2026. The respondents' top concerns included affordability, location & design, and capacity & safety. The respondents' most favored of the housing types were ADUs, cottage courts, and apartment houses.

Mr. Nelson remarked that none of the photos shown in the presentation seemed to represent buildings that might belong on a main street in a quasi-urban environment. Was that potentially part of the scoring showing some people liked some types of buildings in one area and not another? Mr. Vayo felt that was a possibility. Mr. Nelson mentioned that in the TBOD, a zero foot setback is prescribed, which informs the type of buildings that fit in that environment. Mr. Vayo agreed that respondents probably have a sense of this, and it is probably a variable that matters.

Housing types in context were discussed. Respondents favored contexts in the following order: Urban (64.4%), Rural (58.5%) and Suburban (49.5%). Respondents' preferred housing types in each context included live-work and 3-story mixed use in Urban, apartment houses and 3-story mixed use in Suburban, and ADUs and cottage courts in Rural settings.

The existing conditions analysis showed that approximately 70% of households in Derry own their homes. Almost half of the Town's renters are cost-burdened. There are an estimated 9,976 jobs in Derry, making us only second to Manchester in economic power in the region.

Regulations and potential barriers to development in each area were examined. In the Urban area, ground floor residential is prohibited, storefronts are required in mixed use, and the density and dimensional requirements (40 units/acre, 20,000 SF lot, and parking and size) were noted as potential barriers. Commercial uses live and die by exposure; and residential development supports commercial growth. Perhaps there is a potential to hone Derry's zoning regulations to allow storefront requirements to be applied to buildings that front on certain streets.

In the Suburban area, RSA 674:80 and Town amendments are under review (multi-family permissibility), future public sewer, access, and internal streets were noted as potential barriers. Meeting the need for housing while maintaining commercial uses was highlighted. Perhaps storefronts can be placed right along Route 28, with housing on back streets behind the commercial uses.

In the Rural area, 3-acre/200' frontage requirements, permissions for cottage courts and septic capacity, nitrate, and shared access were noted as potential barriers. Bedford's cottage court regulations might be examined.

A limited action item, a targeted change, and a broader framework were provided in the report for each of the three areas.

The final phase of the housing pilot will involve test-fitting select sites within each of the three areas for development potential. This will include starting with an ideal site, applying housing forms, checking the rules, and summarizing tradeoffs. Mr. Vayo offered to return to the Board to present on that final portion.

Mr. Nelson inquired if Woodmont Commons in Londonderry exemplified any of the concepts Mr. Vayo has discussed this evening. Mr. Vayo explained that project was meant to bring in a spectrum of housing and commercial, and that it did not contain any civic or institutional anchors. Projects of that scale carry risk, and this one has endured delays over the years at no fault of the project managers. What has been physically built differs somewhat from the vision laid out, but still meets some of the community's needs. Mr. Vayo has assisted Londonderry with review of their zoning and land use regulations. Mr. Vayo has learned that the scale of the buildings in Woodmont do not meet many Londonderry residents' preferences; this is a good example of why it is important to conduct preference surveys as we are doing in Derry. The cost is often out of reach for current residents, and this has proven to be especially difficult to offset.

Mr. Nelson noted that one of Derry's recent endeavors was a Workforce Housing subcommittee. A local developer that was consulted told the subcommittee that if affordable housing is to be built, every piece of plywood and every nail must be considered. The NH Housing Finance Authority has its own layer of rules. The takeaway was that technical and financial skills are necessary to make affordable housing happen.

Mr. Vayo stated that the most affordable housing is the housing that already exists. To wait and do nothing displaces people that have grown up in Town.

The Board thanked Mr. Vayo for his efforts.

## Planning Director / Chairman Updates

Ms. Robidoux announced that staff's goal is to have the Planning Board member packets ready for pickup on the Monday afternoon before the meeting, so that members have time to color code site plans for improved analysis.

The CART Advisory Board is seeking a voting member; if anyone on the Board or the general public is interested, please reach out to Ms. Robidoux.

Sunoco, 72 Crystal Ave., is repairing and maintaining their underground tanks and sumps. Ms. Robidoux reviewed the plans submitted to the Building Department and determined that the State has jurisdiction over this project and will be handling the permits. No review by the Planning Board is required.

Mr. Nelson thanked all who voted and assisted at the polls at yesterday's general election.

## Public Hearing

*Continued from October 07, 2026*

### Nottonson Family Revocable Trust

**Nottonson Stephen J./Karen E., Trustees**

**PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road**

**Acceptance/Review**

**Two Lot Subdivision**

Ms. Robidoux explained that at the October 7, 2026 meeting, questions were raised as to how this portion of Worthley Road became public. On October 4, 2011 and November 1, 2011, the Derry Town Council held public hearings to determine if occasion existed to layout sections of the Worthley Road right of way. The Council voted to approve and effective December 1, 2011, a 4,362 square foot section of land owned by Stephen and Karen Nottonson (Map 12, Lot 006) became a Class V town approved road. The sections of Worthley below this point were also approved as well. (Copies of the Certificate, minutes and plan were provided to the Board). As noted in the previous staff report, the Nottonson family has frontage on a Class V, town approved road. The ZBA approved a variance to allow the creation of a new lot that would have insufficient frontage.

The Planning Board held a site walk on October 17, 2026. An abutter raised concerns about blasting and effects on neighboring wells. There were also questions about the steep pitch of the driveway and the steep side slopes, and the potential for erosion.

> Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, to reopen the Public Hearing.
>
> All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.

Mr. Nelson stated that during the site walk the Board resolved all questions and concerns from abutters regarding the distinction between the public road, Class V highway, and private right of way. There was discussion about the reconstruction of the right of way proposed to serve also as a driveway. In order to meet Town design standards, there is a fair amount of cuts proposed to move the travel surface away from the public road and keep it at no more than a 15% grade. The slopes of the proposed side cuts are not as much an issue for the Planning Board because they will lie on private property. The only issue would be if additional water flow or sedimentation flow came onto the public roadway. There are no Town Engineering representatives present this evening with which to discuss this.

Neal McCarthy, Promised Land Survey, appeared before the Board.

Mr. McCarthy explained that since there is a cut proposed, there is the potential to create runoff towards the turnabout area. Mr. McCarthy and his team were not able to get the revision done in time to present to the Board this evening. A 2 foot shoulder is proposed on one side, then a three to one slope (which can be secured with seeding) and ending at the bottom in a swale. Going up on the other side, in order to not carry the grading out too much toward the stone wall, there would be a short retaining wall to catch some of the grades. At the end, a little bit of a bowl with rip rap should divert water from going down into the turnabout.

Mr. Nelson invited members of the Board to comment.

Mr. O'Connor mentioned there was a possibility of creating a shared driveway; how is an easement created on top of another easement? Mr. McCarthy explained that there is an easement allowing the Corliss family to pass and repass, so as long as there is no infringement on their right to do so, it should not be a problem. Making the driveway more passable would not infringe on the Corliss' rights and they would be able to use whatever is newly constructed.

Mr. Nelson invited members of the Public to comment.

**Brian Corliss,** 111 Chester Road, was recognized by the Board.

Mr. Corliss provided a timeline of the lot and its subdivision. Mr. Corliss purchased his lot in 1978. In 1985, the lot now known as PID 12006-001 was subdivided by Mr. Corliss from PID 12006. In 2011, the Town created the right of way which extended beyond what Mr. Corliss had done to get the subdivision approved (the "turnabout" area). Mr. Corliss described the right of way's slope as difficult to get up, hazardous to get down, and impossible to get up in the wintertime. Mr. Corliss hoped that if the proposal is approved, that nothing would hinder, interfere with, barricade, or block the Corliss' passage through the right of way. Mr. Corliss acknowledged that Mr. McCarthy's testimony seemed to show that every action will be taken to ensure this.

Mr. Corliss felt the steep slope had to be addressed; adding that concrete mixer trucks would not be able to get up the steep slope to construct the proposed dwelling. Mr. Corliss suggested the Board consider allowing a driveway be constructed off to the side (i.e., a driveway shared up to a certain point with the Nottonsons). Mr. Corliss understands that the Town prefers to not create shared driveways, but mentioned there is a group of three homes on the other side of his lot which share a driveway.

Mr. Nelson stated that Mr. Corliss is referring to potential difficulties that the purchaser of the newly-created lot might have in building a house; therefore those difficulties would belong to the purchaser. Mr. Nelson explained that the Planning Board is concerned with how Mr. Corliss or others aside from the future purchaser may be adversely affected. Mr. Corliss stated that he would not be impacted as long as there are no obstructions to his right of way, and that he can continue to use the right of way. Mr. Corliss understands the desire to build a home in such a lovely spot.

Mr. Corliss' understanding is that a Professional Engineer (PE) will be required to sign off on alterations to the right of way. Mr. Nelson stated that depends; this is a subdivision creating a single new lot. It should be ensured that the Corliss' rights to pass and repass are not infringed upon. That cannot be changed by any action of the Planning Board, but only by a court. The purchaser will extend the driveway to the property line at the maximum slope (≤15%), so there will be a cut with side slopes. The improvements may even cause the right of way to be less steep than it is now in portions, and the Corliss family will not have any lack of access to it. Mr. Corliss was pleased to hear this.

Mr. Corliss added that there are considerations of public utilities along the ROW. Mr. Corliss recalls buying four telephone poles to get electricity to his home, and other utilities have easements on top of the Corliss' ROW.

Mr. Corliss was concerned with water coming down the hill and suggested a catch basin may be needed.

In terms of the steepness of the driving surface, Mr. Nelson stated it is within the Town's regulations. As long as those regulations are maintained, it is not within the Board's power to disallow the proposal. If the side slopes are grassed, rip rapped, or otherwise treated to prevent erosion, and the Town and the abutters do not suffer any injury, then it shall be allowed.

Mr. Corliss commended the Derry DPW for improvements they have made and maintenance they continue to perform on Worthley Road. However, Mr. Corliss remained concerned with the difficulties turning into the slope from the turnabout. Mr. Nelson explained the plans show they are moving it and there would be a flat section added for launch.

Mr. Nelson invited Mr. McCarthy to address Mr. Corliss' concerns. Mr. McCarthy directed the Board's attention to the driveway profile plan and explained how the grading is proposed to meet the regulations. The grading includes a negative slope which is meant to keep water from running into the road. Other than during construction, there will be nothing that will prevent passing and repassing upon the easement.

Mr. McCarthy noted that the construction of the driveway will be the responsibility of the purchaser of the lot. Mr. McCarthy suggested the Board impose a condition of approval requiring a more detailed and expanded cross section plan of the driveway profile plan.

Mr. O'Connor inquired if sheet 4 of 5 captured everything required for the swale and cross sections. Mr. McCarthy said it did not at this time. The final plan would include this and it would be reviewed by Town Engineering prior to the Board signing the plan.

Mr. Pelletier inquired if the plan gave due consideration to emergency vehicle access. Mr. McCarthy stated the driveway as designed conforms to the requirements for a fire engine. Mr. Chase suggested that Mr. Pelletier referred to the lower transition, and not the driveway width. Fire apparatus are fairly long vehicles with low points. The front end could be going up the 14% grade, and the back end could be dragging on the 5% grade. Mr. Chase did not believe that the apparatus would make it up; Mr. Pelletier added that especially Ladder 4 might not make it.

Mr. Nelson wondered if the Town's regulations are not sensitive to meet the current fire engine design standards. Ms. Robidoux explained that as part of the TRC process, the Fire Marshal reviews and signs off on all plans. The only thing that was requested by the Fire Marshal resulting from this project's TRC meeting was that a note be added to the plan with regard to the form of fire protection.

Motion by Pelletier, seconded by Young, to close the Public Hearing.

All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.

Mr. Chase wished to discuss the plan further before granting waivers. Mr. Chase has many issues with a plan requiring a variance in addition to several waivers. Mr. Chase cannot support the waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.A (25) [to allow a driveway to access its lot via an existing access easement and right of way easement rather than through its own frontage] due to Mr. Corliss' testimony and due to the amount of ledge at the location. Mr. McCarthy explained that the frontage for the lot is outside of the paved travel way. Ms. Robidoux suggested that in essence there is a gap between the approved portion of the road and the lot line.

Mr. Nelson's understanding was that the line was the boundary between the accepted public roadway and the parcel under discussion. Mr. Chase believed that the new parcel has a gap between their new lot line and the laid out roadway; Mr. Chase felt this was more than he could support. Mr. Nelson asked if there was a sliver of land between the proposed lot and the lot that will remain to be owner by the Nottonsons; Ms. Robidoux said yes, that is what was meant when referring to the "gap."

Area D, as indicated on the road acceptance plan provided to the Board, indicates the area the Town accepted as a public road. This is technically frontage. In this case, Ms. Robidoux suggested the Board delete the waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.A (25). The suggested waivers were composed prior to the addition of the road acceptance plan to the Board's review materials for this proposal. Mr. Nelson felt deleting this waiver would be appropriate.

Mr. Chase also cannot support the waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.B [to not require the lot sizing to be determined by soil type, but rather by lot area] due to the amount of ledge on the site.

Mr. McCarthy stated that NH DES has approved the subdivision, which is done by lot loading. Mr. Nelson stated that the Town has requirements on soil based sizing, but if the State approves the subdivision, does that mean the Town can't require anything in these regards? Ms. Robidoux explained the State is granting approval that there is ample lot area to support the septic system. Mr. Nelson wondered if the Town should then remove soil based lot sizing from our regulations because the State determines that. Mr. McCarthy stated that the waiver was being requested partly because the lot exceeds three acres, and it would be unusual to not be able to accommodate a septic system on the lot. There are no wetlands on the lot. Soil calculations should still be done for a one acre lot, for example.

Mr. Chase believes that the ledge is right there, and there is documentation that previous blasting resulted in discoloration of water from wells in the area; why should the Board grant something that could be an issue, without any engineering to say that it is not an issue? Mr. Nelson agreed that perhaps that is a waiver that would not be ideal to grant.

Mr. Chase did not have an issue with the waiver being requested from LDCR Section 170-25.A (2) [to not require lot lines to be at substantially right angles to streets].

Mr. Chase felt that the previous and current conversations about the frontage were good reasons to not grant the waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.G [to not require granite bounds to be set at all streets].

Mr. Chase did not have an issue with granting the waiver from LDCR Section 170-26.A (16.a.iv) [to not require a sight distance profile for the new driveway], as this is not a through street.

Mr. Fishman inquired if the Board was concerned that granting the waiver from 170-25.B might result in creating a lot that cannot support a septic system. Ms. Robidoux stated that a building permit cannot be issued unless NH DES approves a septic system design. Mr. McCarthy noted that his firm did a viable test pit on the site as part of NH DES's requirements for granting the subdivision approval. A 44" water table and no ledge were observed within this test pit.

Mr. O'Connor was satisfied with granting the waivers as long as the plan meets all NH DES requirements.

Mr. Minervini was satisfied as long as it meets NH DES requirements; adding that a good portion of the lot is relatively flat, and the lot contains three acres.

Mr. Appleton felt that with a lot this large and with such a significant flat area, it would be unlikely that there would be nowhere on the lot to place a septic system.

Mr. Nelson added that some septic systems are built up / mounded due to the presence of ledge on the site.

Regarding the granite bounds, Mr. Fishman felt that given the confusion, it would be worthwhile to install granite bounds. Mr. O'Connor suggested allowing granite or iron / galvanized rebar. Mr. Nelson stated that those were the only two options, and for front lot lines, the Board usually requires granite.

Mr. McCarthy explained this waiver was requested because there is an RSA forbidding the removal of existing monuments or things that are deeded. There are stonewalls on site where monuments would sit which they would prefer not to disturb, but they would install granite bounds where possible. A drill hole or round plate would be used on the portions at existing stonewalls.

Mr. Nelson asked the Board if there were objections to modifying the waiver to not require granite bounds where existing boundary markers would be statutorily impacted at the street; there were no objections.

No members of the Board expressed any concerns with the waiver from LDCR Section 170-26.A (16.a.iv), sight distance.

Motion by Pelletier, seconded by Young, to grant a waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.B to not require the lot sizing to be determined by soil type, but rather by lot area. After review of the waiver request, the Board finds that strict conformity to the regulations would pose an unnecessary hardship to the applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and intent of the regulations.

Roll Call Vote: Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. Chase and Pelletier voted No; given the topography and the way the lot is laid out, the lot should have been determined by soil. The motion passed.

Motion by Pelletier, seconded by Yyoung, to grant a waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.A (2) to not require lot lines to be at substantially right angles to streets. After review of the waiver request, the Board finds that strict conformity to the regulations would pose an unnecessary hardship to the applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and intent of the regulations.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

Motion by Pelletier, seconded by Young, to grant a waiver from LDCR Section 170-26.A (16.a.iv) to not require a sight distance profile for the new driveway. After review of the waiver request, the Board finds that strict conformity to the regulations would pose an unnecessary hardship to the applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and intent of the regulations.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

Motion by Chirichiello, seconded by Young, to grant a waiver from LDCR Section 170-25.G to not require granite bounds where existing boundary markers would be statutorily impacted at the street. After review of the waiver request, the Board finds that strict conformity to the regulations would pose an unnecessary hardship to the applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and intent of the regulations.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

The Board finds the proposed plan provides safe and efficient vehicular access, and the design and construction of the access ways is adequate to accommodate the anticipated volume of traffic proposed by the development.

The Board finds erosion and sediment control provisions are adequate.

Mr. Nelson suggested that since the Board discussed erosion and sediment control that was not yet depicted on the plan, perhaps it could be made a condition. Ms. Robidoux confirmed that a finding of fact cannot be conditioned; the suggested motion relates to the sediment and erosion control that was already on the plan.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, the Board makes Findings of Fact, as listed above.

Roll Call Vote: Minervini, O'Connor, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. Chase and Appleton voted No, as they have not seen any plan for erosion control for new cut driveway. The motion passed.

Mr. Chirichiello expressed concern that the construction of the new lot's driveway could impede the Corliss' ability to access their easement. Mr. Nelson suggested that, during construction, there may be a period of time (perhaps a week?) that the Corliss family cannot use the easement. Mr. Chirichiello has an issue with this. Mr. Nelson felt it was outside the Board's jurisdiction. Ms. Robidoux stated there is already a recorded easement that the Corliss family and then anyone who purchases the lot thereafter has the right to pass and repass.

Ms. Robidoux suggested that good neighbors would do what they could to not block the access during construction, and it was not anything the Board had legal authority over. Mr. Chirichiello felt that was good in theory, but it was unknown if the new owner would be different. If the new owner of the lot approaches the Corliss family and asks if it is ok to temporarily block the access, and the Corlisses are ok with that, then that would be fine by Mr. Chirichiello. Mr. McCarthy felt that the work to this access would be significant. Ms. Robidoux did not feel that the Board had the authority to alter existing easements between private properties. Ms. Robidoux added that typically buyers will review the approved plan prior to purchasing; and it will be on the forefront of staff's minds to pass the message along at the time of application for a driveway permit. The new lot's deed will reflect the Corliss' easement, so when they close on the property, the new owners would be well aware of it. ## Richard J. Ward

### PID 10007-001, 190 Hampstead Road

**Acceptance/Review**

**Two Lot Subdivision**

Ms. Robidoux explained the property is located in the Low Medium Density Residential district which requires a 2 acre minimum and 150 feet of frontage. The existing lot contains 5 acres. The proposed subdivision creates a 2.22 acre lot with 350.62 feet of frontage, leaving the parent lot at 2.78 acres and 438.5 feet of frontage.

The new lot is encumbered by 14,216 sf of wetland and an area of encroachment to the rear of the lot by the Drew Woods Condominium Association. The new lot will be serviced by onsite well and septic and will not connect to the Pennichuck Water system, similar to the parent lot. A fire hydrant is located near the top of Village Brook Lane. Other utilities include underground electric and data, and a propane tank. A 15" HDPE driveway culvert will be installed in the DOT right of way to maintain the existing drainage patterns along the roadway.

All TRC comments were addressed, and the Conservation Commission reviewed and signed the plan. It appears the stonewall to the front is the front property line. Care should be taken to preserve

any monumentation in that wall for the future. Mr. Nelson added that if the stone wall is the boundary, no stones shall be taken from the wall per State law.

A NH DOT Driveway Permit and a NH DES Subdivision approval will be required.

Staff recommends the Board review the plan and make a determination with regard to Regional Impact.

Motion by Minervini, seconded by Pelletier, to accept jurisdiction of the 2 lot subdivision plan before the Board for Richard Ward, PID 10007-001, 190 Hampstead Road.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, and Nelson vote Yes. Mr. O'Connor was out of the room at the time of this motion. The motion passed.

Motion by Chase, seconded by Pelletier, pursuant to RSA 36:56, the Board finds the proposal as presented at this time meets the definition of a development of regional impact.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Appleton, Minervini, Fishman, Chirichiello, Pelletier, Young, O'Connor, and Nelson vote No, this is a minor two lot subdivision in the center of Town and it does not impede any utilities, traffic flow, etc., therefore it does not meet the definition of a development of regional impact.

Motion by Pelletier, seconded by Young, to open the Public Hearing.

All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.

Pete Madsen of Keach Nordstrom Associates and Tyler Brissenden of TJB Homes were recognized by the Board.

Mr. Madsen explained the lot currently contains a single family dwelling. The applicant seeks to subdivide the property to create another lot for a single family dwelling. The new lot will be a little under 2.25 acres, and the remaining lot will be a little over 2.75 acres. The existing lot is serviced by private septic and well, and the same will be true for the new lot. There is an existing isolated wetland pocket that was identified by Bruce Gilday, CWS.

The new dwelling is a proposed 4-bedroom single family home with a 130 linear foot driveway off of Hampstead Road. Proposed limits of clearing have been depicted on the plan, and wildlife friendly erosion control measures will be used around the areas of disturbance, per request of the Conservation Commission. There are no proposed impacts to wetlands or to wetland buffers.

Hampstead Road is under NHDOT jurisdiction, and 400' of sight distance from the driveway is required and has been provided. A driveway application has been submitted to NHDOT. The NH DES subdivision application was approved last week.

Mr. Madsen mentioned that the abutters at 1 Wishing Well Lane expressed concern to Ms. Robidoux that there might be a stream in the front right corner of the lot. Mr. Madsen explained that Mr. Gilday went back out to the site last week; Mr. Gilday determined there is no jurisdictional wetland in that location.

Mr. Nelson asked if NHDOT indicated they would be issuing a driveway permit; Mr. Madsen said that he had no reason to believe that NHDOT would not issue the permit, but that the process takes some time.

Regarding wetlands, Mr. O'Connor mentioned that the Conservation Commission had signed off on the plan.

**Jack Webb**, 25 Drew Woods Drive, was recognized by the Board. (Mr. Webb noted that the Chamberlains, 23 Drew Woods Drive, Mr. Wendell, 21 Drew Woods Drive, and Mr. Brophy, 19 Drew Woods Drive were also present this evening.)

Mr. Webb expressed that these abutters' main concern is drainage. There are wetlands which serve as part of the Drew Woods development's drainage. Drainage swales exist in front of almost all of the houses. Catch basins which discharge into retention ponds in various locations in the neighborhood also exist. The neighborhood experiences areas which are seasonally wet. The concern is that impervious space (dwelling, pavement, etc.) added to the new lot might result in worsened runoff for the Drew Woods development.

Mr. Nelson added that generally the post-development runoff conditions shall not exceed the pre-development runoff conditions.

**Will Davison and Brenda Davison**, 1 Wishing Well Lane, were recognized by the Board.

Mr. Davison stated that he and his wife echo the runoff concerns of the Drew Woods abutters. Mr. Davison felt that the surface area being created will cause more water to drain to the left to his property. Mr. Davison mentioned there is also a pond across the street at 187 Hampstead Road which drains from across the street and into his property.

Mr. Davison is concerned that clear cutting may go right up to the property line and not maintain the 15' no cut buffer, which could result in runoff coming directly into his property.

Mr. Davison requested if the plan is approved, that the underground utilities be moved to the other side of the new driveway so as not to disturb the root systems of the Davisons' trees.

Mr. Madsen responded that they were under the threshold for providing permanent drainage facilities on the site. They are proposing temporary erosion control measures, and perimeter controls which the Conservation Commission requested. In terms of runoff, a single family home with a relatively short driveway does not typically generate a significant amount of runoff. The tree line is proposed to remain at the 15' building setback. Mr. Madsen felt that, relatively, there was not a lot of clearing proposed for the site. There is a desire to have a front yard area for the new house. Otherwise, the limits of disturbance are minor. A drainage memo has been submitted to the Board to that effect. Additionally, the team has added a driveway culvert at the request of the Department of Public Works. The existing 12" RCP will also be cleaned out by the site crew.

Mr. Nelson inquired about the location of the underground utilities. Mr. Madsen explained that Eversource does not typically get involved with the preapproval process. Mr. Madsen is glad to move the proposed location of the utilities to the other side of the new driveway, but ultimately Eversource will determine the location.

Mr. Davison thought that the location of the electrical panel in the home would determine the direction the power is brought into the building. Mr. Nelson stated that would only be part of the consideration. Mr. Nelson agreed that Mr. Madsen can suggest the location, but Eversource would have the final say. The Planning Board does not have any jurisdiction over the location of electrical panels in buildings.

Mr. Davison inquired about the direction of the slope that will be created by the installation of the new culvert. Mr. Madsen stated that it would be going toward the Davison's property, but it will not be adding additional flow, but conveying existing flow that runs off of Hampstead Road.

Mr. Davison stated that when the wetland is saturated and overflows, it doesn't flow toward his property. Mr. Davison suggested that if a culvert is placed there, it will allow the overflow to be directed more naturally into his property, and then go back into Drew Woods. Mr. Madsen said the driveway culvert does not interact with that existing wetland; it's a protection measure required by the Town for all driveways.

Ms. Davison wished to confirm that the vegetation will not be cleared all the way up to her property line. While this is a conceptual plan, the intent is to maintain vegetation in the 15' buffer. Mr. Brissenden will be developing the property.

Mr. Brissenden confirmed that he is amenable to what is being discussed this evening and he has no problem leaving the 15' buffer. In NH, people favor wooded lots; Mr. Brissenden prefers to leave as much vegetation as possible.

Ms. Davison inquired if the Town would audit the culvert to ensure it can withstand the increased water flow going across Hampstead Road into her property. Ms. Davison added that the business at 187 Hampstead Road causes extra water to come across the road to her property. Mr. Madsen stated that the driveway culvert does not convey any additional runoff; it's just a safety measure to promote the existing flow already being generated from Hampstead Road.

Mr. Chirichiello inquired if the parcel was within the 100-year flood zone. Mr. Madsen stated this parcel is not in a flood zone.

Mr. Nelson explained that he cannot guarantee the DPW would audit the new culvert, but they will inspect it.

Ms. Davison inquired if the wetland scientist went on her property last week. Mr. Madsen explained that the scientist would have only gone on the subject parcel. Ms. Davison inquired if the wetland scientist determined if there were wetlands on her own property. Mr. Madsen stated that was not a determination that was required to be made; the wetland scientist only looked at the subject parcel.

**Evelyn Wendell**, 21 Drew Woods Drive, was recognized by the Board.

Ms. Wendell wished to express that there is some water displacement from the subject parcel onto her parcel.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Pelletier, to close the Public Hearing.

All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.
